messages:
anya: Heads up: saw a staging repro where an eviction applied after a lease revoke and clients hit tombstones. Short logs below.

sam: Can you paste the minimal log lines?

anya: ```
[2026-03-22T17:10:12Z] lease_revoke epoch=321 prefix=svc/X
[2026-03-22T17:10:12Z] evict_decide epoch=320 prefix=svc/X node=node-5
[2026-03-22T17:10:12Z] client_read -> tombstone
```

anya: Root cause: eviction apply path sometimes uses stale epoch observations taken at schedule time. fanout latency meant revoke not seen before apply.

tess: Options: (A)always re-read meta at apply (safe, extra RTT); (B)add revoke fence token + epoch-check (meta field + queue semantics).

kai: Hybrid proposal: enqueue a revoke-fence (high priority) on revoke + apply-time cheap epoch read from local meta cache; on mismatch retry/backoff. Fence reduces common-case races; epoch-check guarantees safety.

sam: Perf concerns: ensure local meta-cache invalidation on fanout so reads are cheap. Add metrics evict_skipped_epoch and evict_applied_after_revoke; alert if applied_after_revoke > 0.1%.

tess: Test plan: unit + chaos (inject fanout delays), sim harness for N=1e6 ops. rollout via feature flag canary 10% then 50%.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary started region=us-west-2 flag=evict_epoch_check=true pct=10

anya: I'll open RFC with split/merge epoch semantics and perf numbers. Link when ready.
